title: introduce-tenant-scoped-gpu-lease-tf-modules-and-state-concat
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Private deployments increasingly require per-tenant isolation for GPU capacity and state. Current Terraform layout stores shared pools and global TFState keys which makes per-tenant imports and rolling updates risky and noisy. This PR adds tenant-scoped GPU lease modules, a state-concatenation keying pattern, and a state migrator script to safely split existing global state without downtime.

What this PR introduces (high level): 1) module/tenant-gpu-lease: a new TF module that provisions a lightweight lease controller, dedicated nodepool shims, and IAM bindings scoped to a tenant identifier. The lease controller is implemented as a CRD-enabled bootstrap (cloud-init + systemd unit) that marks capacity as "leased" in a DynamoDB-style lock table (provider-agnostic key-value table resource). 2) state_key concatenation: we introduce a consistent state key pattern tfstate/<env>/<tenant>/<component> so each tenant's GPU/nodepool lifecycle is decoupled from the global compute state. 3) lock sharding and migrator: a small Go migrator (scripts/tfstate-migrator.go) that runs in dry-run mode to map existing resources into tenant states and orchestrates remote state copies with lock handoff to avoid double-apply. 4) IAM least-privilege templates: new iam/nodepool-role module with narrower permissions for node bootstrap and HSM/KMS envelope unwrap permissions. 5) Networking isolation helpers: per-tenant subnet route table attachments, optional VPC peering keys and route selectors to support on-prem isolation. 6) upgrade/rollback plan and docs: scripts/upgrade-plan.md and rollback instructions for safe rerolls.

Why this is different than previous refactors: instead of splitting nodepools by AZ or GPU label, this change focuses on tenant scoping and introducing a composable state keying pattern that can be adopted incrementally per-tenant. The migrator provides a safe migration path with a native dry-run and reconciliation loop.

Compatibility and rollout: The modules are opt-in. Existing deployments remain unchanged unless the env-level config toggles tenant_mode = true and maps tenant IDs. The migrator supports partial migration: you can pick a single tenant and move its compute resources to a new state key. The plan supports automatic fallback: if post-migration smoke tests fail, the migrator can reverse the operation and rehydrate the original state.

Testing and CI: terratest suite added for module/tenant-gpu-lease which runs with a local emulator for the key-value lock table and a mocked cloud provider for nodepool APIs. CI initially failed because of fmt/validate issues; those were fixed in followup commits. The PR passed the full pipeline and a manual canary in staging with a single-tenant migration.

Files touched (high level): module/tenant-gpu-lease/*, module/iam/nodepool-role/*, scripts/tfstate-migrator.go, scripts/upgrade-plan.md, examples/tenant-migration/{main.tf,vars.tf}, charts/installer/values-tenant.yaml, docs/private/tenant-state-concat.md

Release notes: Adds opt-in tenant-scoped GPU lease modules and a safe TFState migrator for per-tenant state decomposition. This enables isolated upgrades and per-tenant capacity billing.

review_comments: Connor Patel: Can we avoid adding any provider-specific DynamoDB resources in the module? Suggest abstracting the lock-table interface so customers can choose native cloud TTL tables or our existing k/v service.
Maya Chen (author): Good point — converted lock table to a provider-agnostic 'kv_table' abstraction and added adapters for aws_dynamodb_table and a local file-backed stub used by tests.

Elena Rivera: The IAM template looks ok but we need to ensure the role cannot assume broad compute permissions. Please restrict iam:List* actions and add a comment explaining the minimal set used for node bootstrap.
Maya Chen (author): tightened policy and added explanatory comments with least-privilege rationale. Also added an integration unit test that verifies no wildcard in actions.
Samir Gupta: The migrator is powerful; include explicit user prompts and dry-run as default to reduce accidental runs. Also add telemetry metrics for migration duration and failure rates.
Maya Chen (author): made dry-run default and added optional --apply flag. Added Prometheus metrics export hooks and documented them in scripts/upgrade-plan.md.
merge_commit: 7f8d2a1 merged tenant-scoped GPU lease modules and tfstate migrator
ci_log_summary: Initial pipeline failed on terraform fmt and a terratest mock gap. Follow-up fixes addressed fmt, provider pin, and added test stubs. Full pipeline passed including terratest against the local kv emulator.
release_notes: Opt-in tenant-scoped GPU lease terraform modules, state-key concatenation pattern, and a safe tfstate migrator for per-tenant decomposition. Includes IAM least-privilege templates and network isolation helpers.
notes_for_ops: Operators should review scripts/upgrade-plan.md before running migrator in production. Recommended steps: run dry-run for a single tenant in staging, validate canary workloads, then run --apply with a maintenance window. Monitor migration metrics exposed by the migrator. Backups: ensure existing remote state snapshots are stored before apply.
testing_instructions: See examples/tenant-migration for an end-to-end scenario. Run: make test-tenant-migration which boots the local kv emulator, runs terraform init/plan/apply against the example with tenant_mode=true, and then executes terratest. Use MIGRATOR_DRY_RUN=1 for an explicit dry-run.
